entries.test: Documented film productions replacing filmmakers with Sora, including evidence of whether its practical limitations prevented that replacement.
entries.note: The prediction has no deadline; its causal explanation is also part of the assertion.
The proposition drops 'entirely.' Neither the bubble nor its dependence on public acceptance has a shared operational meaning here.

entries.test: Contemporaneous reliability evaluations, compute and power costs, and documented economically viable deployments at scale of Sora and comparable generative AI products.
entries.note: The cost assertion concerns May 2024, and its sweeping exclusion of at-scale use is testable.

entries.test: Documented useful filmmaking deployments of Sora and measurements establishing whether they required the stated precision, hallucination and processing improvements.
entries.note: These are asserted necessary conditions, not a promise that improvements would suffice.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures or credible cost reporting on ChatGPT's operating profitability and Sora's operating costs and model complexity in May 2024.
entries.note: This concerns product operating economics, not simply OpenAI's overall profitability.

entries.test: Contemporaneous OpenAI product evaluations and operating-cost evidence showing whether precision, hallucination and compute-cost limitations remained unresolved.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph identifies the problems being referenced.

entries.test: Public reporting on OpenAI's late-2023 Microsoft efficiency project and reproducible task comparisons between GPT-4 and its predecessor.
entries.note: Both components are factual historical assertions.

entries.test: Published learning experiments and hallucination research testing the asserted absence of learning ability and its claimed causal connection to hallucinations.
entries.note: The categorical denial of any ability to learn is empirically assessable even though consciousness is contested.

entries.test: Public GPT-4 infrastructure reporting, GPU prices and inference-cost measurements showing how computation contributes to serving costs.

entries.note: 'Repurposing Playwright' does not establish that the entire model is merely repurposed scripts. The parenthetical confirmation nevertheless conveys endorsement of the core implementation claim.

entries.test: Public security audits or authenticated implementation details showing whether Rabbit must retain recoverable original credentials instead of only password hashes or delegated tokens.

The proposition omits 'every ounce' and the recent-weeks scope. Bad or unsophisticated design is an evaluative conclusion here.

entries.test: Contemporaneous independent trials and launch footage showing completion rates for the Large Action Model's advertised tasks.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'looks like.' Despite the insult, the passage commits to a practical claim about very limited functionality.

entries.test: Playwright's public source code and documentation establishing whether the scripting framework itself implements AI.
entries.note: The referent is Playwright itself, not every component that might call it.

entries.test: Documented supported-site layout or workflow changes and corresponding Rabbit integration behavior showing whether the affected service breaks and requires code changes.

entries.note: Later additions would not refute a claim about the device at publication.

entries.test: Contemporaneous coverage, preorder records and public purchaser research linking inadequate reporting of the Large Action Model to the approximately ten thousand purchases.

This prescribes how companies should be reviewed and criticized.

entries.test: Publicly available agent demonstrations and evaluations as of May 2024 showing the strength of evidence for reliable assistants that operate users' apps.

entries.test: Contemporaneous autonomous-agent capabilities and historical documentation of document-question-answering systems establishing whether the characterization and decade-old comparison hold.
